newsitem.title: UK: Med oil products steady, except stronger gas oil.
newsitem.headline: Med oil products steady, except stronger gas oil.

text.p: Mediterranean oil products were steady except for marginally firmer gas oil on Friday, traders said.
Gasoline was steady in tight supply due to refinery spring maintenance. Traders said that while end-user demand remained slack some light trade short-covering was supporting prices.
This stirred some interest to move product from the better supplied NWE market, but traders said that freight costs and the possibility of transatlantic trade were restricted possibilities.
Cargoes valued around $220 a tonne cif Med.

Saudi Aramco decided not to award its tender for up to 1.5 million barrels of gasoline for April delivery as offers were too high, traders said. Some of the product had been expected to be sourced in Europe due to tight Far East supplies. However, one trader said Aramco may now defer its requirements to May.
Russian gas oil prices firmed in the Med, with the market tightened by buying into India. Two cargoes were on offer at quotes cif high +$2/$3 a tonne, with one heard traded at +$2.
Traders said that barrels were scarce with shorts seen into the south of France, Malta, the Canary Islands and Lebanon, all for March delivery.
"The promptish barrels for March are quite hard to find," a trader said.
The market for Italian gas oil was seen steady, with a $10 a tonne differential holding between heating oil and diesel.

Low sulphur fuel oil was quiet on Friday with little interest being shown by the main buyer. Prices were unchanged around $100 cif Med, but may be knocked lower on good avails of transatlantic cargoes.
High sulphur cracked fuel was helped by movement to the Far East. Trading sources and shipbrokers said upwards of 250,000 tonnes was fixed for March loadings to Fujairah and Singapore.
